In Nehemiah 5:14-15, we see a leader who, even with authority and position, chose to remain faithful to God. Nehemiah 5:15 (NIV) says:
"But the earlier governors—those preceding me—placed a heavy burden on the people and took from them food and wine, besides forty shekels of silver. Their assistants also lorded it over the people. But out of reverence for God I did not act like that."

This attitude teaches us that true fear of the Lord transforms our choices, our character, and the way we treat others. Nehemiah could have used his position for personal gain, but he chose to honor God above the benefits he could receive.

In the same way, we need to be transformed through repentance and through the grace that is found only in Jesus Christ. We must turn our hearts back to God through the reading of His Word and through prayer, seeking daily the grace of Christ. And, as Jesus commanded in the Great Commission, we must not keep this truth to ourselves, but take the Gospel to others, proclaiming the hope we have received.

text:
I was the “Preeti” in someone’s life back then. When I saw those messages...the longing in his heart for her, the way he was still waiting for her to come back...that’s when I realized that she was still in his heart, even after all this time. And I knew that the place and the kind of love he had for her were things I could never have😅😅

That very moment, I told him, You should be with her. You should go back to her. She is the one you love. I was only brought into your life to fill the empty space she left behind, to ease your loneliness.

I told him, Go to her. I won’t be angry. What hurts me is that you’re neither going to her nor truly making me yours.

And when you have someone else running through your mind while you’re with me, then please, choose her. Because my conscience tells me that when someone is constantly comparing you to another person, your value in their heart was already lower to begin with. So never, even by mistake, try or wish to become someone’s first choice when you know their heart has already placed someone else above you.

Still, he stayed with me. For a while, I genuinely believed that he wanted to make me his, wholeheartedly. But a few months later, I realized that no😄😄he wasn’t going to be able to forget her.

I realized it through the way he started talking to me, the growing distance between us, and the emotional unavailability that became impossible to ignore. I was the person he felt he had to choose because he didn’t want to hurt me, but I was not the person he had chosen with his whole heart.

So, for the last time, I told him, Please don’t stay with me out of pity. I’m not hurt. Just go😊
